newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Former Yeltsin aide turned critic wins seat.
newsitem.headline: Former Yeltsin aide turned critic wins seat.

text.p: General Alexander Korzkhakov, a former close aide of President Boris Yeltsin and now one of his fiercest opponents, launched his political career by winning a seat in the Russian parliament on Monday.

The electoral commission in the central Russian city of Tula said preliminary results gave Yeltsin's one-time bodyguard Korzhakov 26 percent of Sunday's vote, more than nine points clear of his nearest rival, local politician Eduard Pashchenko.
Another celebrity in the race, chess champion Anatoly Karpov, was just behind in third place.
Nikolai Novikov, a businessman who ran his campaign from a prison cell while awaiting trial for extortion, was fourth. He denies the extortion charges.
The other six candidates in the field were far behind.
The Tula seat fell vacant when popular general Alexander Lebed was brought into the Kremlin last June as Yeltsin's security chief.
Lebed, sacked in October, first backed Korzhakov in the election race but then distanced himself from the burly 47-year-old, calling him "a mere bodyguard".
Korzhakov, a close friend of Yeltsin's for 10 years, has presented himself as a victim of a Kremlin plot and pledged to make public "compromising material" against the establishment.
